name: Regal Rexnord
desc: Makes electric motors, power transmission components, bearings and automation products for HVAC, industrial, aerospace and agricultural customers.
markets: Manufacturing, sales and service across the US, Canada, Mexico, Europe and Asia; industrial customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B engineering brand could use F1 for motion-control technology showcase and customer hospitality; little consumer marketing tradition.
changed: Formed in 2021 by merger of Regal Beloit with Rexnord's process and motion control business

name: Olam Agri
desc: Originates, processes and trades grains, rice, edible oils, flour, animal feed and cotton for food manufacturers and consumers.
markets: Sourcing and processing in Africa and Asia; sells to food and feed manufacturers and consumers across emerging markets and globally.
rationale: Commodity trader focused on emerging markets with little brand marketing in core F1 markets; weak F1 fit.
changed: Saudi Arabia's SALIC bought 35.4% in 2022 and agreed in 2025 to raise its stake to about 80% (completion not confirmed)

name: International Holding Company
desc: Abu Dhabi holding company owning businesses in real estate, healthcare, food, utilities, construction, finance, technology and mining.
markets: Core holdings in the UAE, with investments across the Middle East, Africa, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Large Abu Dhabi group with sports and entertainment interests; F1 could support Gulf corporate hospitality and international profile.

name: Mowi
desc: Farms, processes and sells Atlantic salmon and seafood products to supermarkets, food service companies and distributors.
markets: Farms in Norway, Scotland, Canada, Chile, Ireland, Faroe Islands and Iceland; sells in about 70 markets including Europe, US and Asia.
rationale: Mostly B2B seafood supplier with a growing consumer brand in Europe; plausible but not obvious F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from Marine Harvest to Mowi in 2019

name: Olam Group (formerly Olam International)
desc: Agri-business group sourcing, processing and trading cocoa, coffee, nuts, spices, dairy, grains, rice and cotton for food manufacturers.
markets: Operates in around 60 countries, supplying food, beverage and industrial manufacturers worldwide through ofi and Olam Agri.
rationale: B2B ingredients and commodity supplier with low consumer awareness; F1 fit is weak beyond corporate hospitality.
changed: Restructured in 2022 into Olam Group with ofi and Olam Agri; Olam International became a subsidiary of listed Olam Group

name: Syngenta Group
desc: Sells crop protection chemicals, seeds, and digital farming tools to farmers and distributors through Syngenta, Adama and Syngenta Group China.
markets: Sells to farmers and distributors in over 100 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Global agritech brand known to farmers but not consumers; F1 could serve B2B hospitality and innovation messaging, though state ownership complicates.
changed: Syngenta AG acquired by ChemChina in 2017; Syngenta Group formed in 2020; Shanghai IPO withdrawn in 2024

name: Corteva Agriscience
desc: Develops and sells seeds under Pioneer and Brevant and crop protection products such as herbicides, insecticides and biologicals.
markets: Sells to farmers and distributors in more than 110 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa.
rationale: Strong farmer brand but almost no consumer reach; F1 could support B2B hospitality and science messaging, plausible not obvious.
changed: Spun off from DowDuPont in 2019; announced in 2025 a plan to separate seed and crop protection businesses (completion not confirmed)

name: John Deere (Deere & Company)
desc: Manufactures tractors, combines, construction and forestry equipment, lawn care machines and precision agriculture technology, plus equipment financing.
markets: Dealer network and factories across North America, South America, Europe, India, China and Australia.
rationale: Iconic machinery brand with autonomy and precision technology to showcase; F1 offers global dealer hospitality and engineering storytelling.

name: ICL Group
desc: Produces potash, phosphates, bromine, magnesium, specialty fertilisers and food and industrial ingredients from Dead Sea and other mines.
markets: Production in Israel, Spain, the UK, US, China and elsewhere; sells to agriculture, food and industrial customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B minerals and chemicals producer with little consumer marketing; weak F1 fit beyond customer hospitality.

name: Glencore
desc: Mines and trades copper, cobalt, nickel, zinc, coal and other commodities, and markets oil, for industrial buyers worldwide.
markets: Mining and trading operations across Africa, the Americas, Australia, Europe and Asia; customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B commodity group with coal and oil exposure that raises sponsorship sensitivities; weak F1 fit.
changed: Agricultural arm Viterra, about half-owned by Glencore, merged into Bunge in 2025

name: Zoomlion Heavy Industry
desc: Manufactures concrete machinery, cranes, earthmoving equipment, aerial work platforms and agricultural machinery for contractors and farmers.
markets: Largest market is China, with growing exports to Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Latin America and Europe, including Italian CIFA.
rationale: Chinese machinery maker expanding overseas could use F1 for international brand building and dealer hospitality; plausible.

name: ARAUCO (Celulosa Arauco y Constitución)
desc: Produces pulp, sawn timber, wood panels and bioenergy from plantations, selling to construction, furniture and packaging industries.
markets: Forestry and mills in Chile, Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay, panel plants in North America; exports to Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Industrial wood and pulp producer with B2B customers and little consumer branding; weak F1 fit.

name: OCP Group
desc: Mines phosphate rock and produces phosphoric acid and fertilisers, exporting to farmers in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.
markets: Exports from Morocco to Africa, South Asia, Europe and the Americas, with subsidiaries and joint ventures abroad.
rationale: State-owned national champion with sports sponsorship history; F1 could support Moroccan and African profile, plausible not obvious.

name: Dow
desc: Makes plastics, packaging materials, industrial intermediates, coatings and silicones for packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer-care customers.
markets: Manufacturing and customers in over 100 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Materials maker with a past Olympic partnership; F1 offers lightweighting and sustainability tech showcase and B2B hospitality.

name: Yara International
desc: Produces and sells nitrogen fertilisers, ammonia, industrial nitrogen products and digital farming tools to farmers, distributors and industry.
markets: Production sites on six continents and sales in more than 60 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa.
rationale: B2B fertiliser brand known in agriculture only; F1 offers limited value beyond decarbonisation messaging; weak fit.

name: Dangote Group
desc: Nigerian conglomerate producing cement, sugar, salt, flour, fertiliser and refined petroleum products for African consumers and builders.
markets: Mainly Nigeria, with cement plants and sales in other African countries and fuel and fertiliser exports.
rationale: Highly visible African brand that sponsors sport; F1 could build its international profile, though markets are mostly African.
changed: Dangote Petroleum Refinery at Lekki began production in 2024

name: Marubeni
desc: Japanese general trading house active in grain, food, power, infrastructure, metals, chemicals, aerospace and other businesses through trading and investments.
markets: Operations and investments in dozens of countries across Asia, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global trading house with B2B relationships could use F1 for corporate hospitality; plausible but not obvious.

name: Trimble
desc: Sells positioning hardware, software and sensors for construction, surveying and geospatial work to contractors, engineers and surveyors.
markets: Sells across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific to construction, geospatial and engineering customers.
rationale: Precision positioning and digital construction technology could be showcased via F1 engineering partnership and B2B hospitality.
changed: Agriculture business moved into PTx Trimble joint venture with AGCO (AGCO majority) in 2024

name: Wilmar International
desc: Agribusiness group processing and trading palm oil, edible oils, sugar, rice, flour and oilseeds, selling branded consumer foods in Asia.
markets: Plantations in Indonesia and Malaysia, processing across China, India, Southeast Asia and Africa; consumer brands such as Arawana in China.
rationale: Strong Asian consumer food brands but little marketing in core F1 markets; plausible for Asian brand building.
